statement: Running `scaffold-project.sh --records-cutover <dir>` on a project whose `.trd-state/<slug>/` run records are tracked first writes the framework ignore lines into `.gitignore`, then removes from the index every path `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard -- .trd-state` listed, printing one `Untracked <path>` line per path
cites: lines 40-44; lines 5-9 (the lines are delivered but nothing untracks them today); lines 21-22
evidence: Transcript of the command in a fixture repo with tracked records: the `.gitignore` diff showing `.trd-state/*`, one `Untracked .trd-state/<slug>/implement.json` line per listed path, and `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard -- .trd-state` printing nothing afterwards

statement: The untracking is index-only and staged: every untracked file is still present on disk with its content unchanged, and `git status` shows each as a staged deletion
cites: line 42 ("`git rm --cached`, staged, never committed")
evidence: Transcript: `git status --porcelain` lines `D  .trd-state/<slug>/...` for each path, and `ls`/`sha256sum` of the same files before and after showing identical hashes

statement: The whole cutover (untracking and seeding) creates no commit: `HEAD` of the target worktree and of every other worktree is the same commit before and after `--records-cutover`
cites: line 42 ("never committed"); line 15 and line 36 (`fallback: false` never commits and never folds)
evidence: Transcript: `git rev-parse HEAD` in each worktree and `git log --oneline -1 --all` before and after the run, identical

statement: `.trd-state/_docs-audit/` files stay tracked through the cutover: none is printed as `Untracked`, and each is still in `git ls-files` afterwards
cites: lines 5-6 (the `!.trd-state/_docs-audit/` exception); lines 21-22 (the listing honours that negation)
evidence: Transcript in a fixture repo holding a tracked `.trd-state/_docs-audit/<file>`: no `Untracked .trd-state/_docs-audit/` line, and `git ls-files .trd-state/_docs-audit/` still listing the file

statement: No other scaffold mode untracks a run record: after `scaffold-project.sh --refresh`, a plain `scaffold-project.sh`, and `scaffold-project.sh --git-files`, each run on a repo with tracked `.trd-state/<slug>/` records, those records are still tracked
cites: line 44-45 ("No other mode untracks a record"); lines 10-11 (`--git-files` untracks only the scratch lines above the marker)
evidence: Three transcripts, one per mode, each followed by `git ls-files .trd-state/<slug>/` still listing the record files and `git status --porcelain` showing no `D` entry for them

statement: `/rebase-project` runs the cutover as Step 4.7b, immediately after Step 4.7a, by invoking `scaffold-project.sh --records-cutover`; a `/rebase-project` run on a project with tracked records leaves them untracked (staged) and seeds the in-flight feature's ref
cites: line 46
evidence: The Step 4.7b text in `rebase-project.md` placed right after 4.7a and naming `--records-cutover`; and a headless `/rebase-project` session transcript in a fixture slot followed by `git status --porcelain` (staged `D` lines) and `git show-ref refs/ensemble/records/<slug>`

statement: The `/rebase-project` report lists the files it untracked, the refs it seeded and the features it skipped
cites: lines 46-47
evidence: The final readout of a headless `/rebase-project` fixture run naming an untracked `.trd-state/...` path, the seeded `refs/ensemble/records/<slug>`, and a skipped slug with its reason

statement: The `/rebase-project` Rollback section says how to undo the staged removals and states that a pushed ref is not undone by `git restore`
cites: lines 47-48
evidence: The Rollback section text of `rebase-project.md` carrying both statements

statement: `node records-cutover.js seed` prints exactly one line of JSON with `ok`, `seeded` (entries with `slug`, `worktree`, `branch`, `ref`, `commit`, `push`) and `skipped` (entries with `slug`, `worktree`, `reason`), and exits 0
cites: lines 30-32
evidence: Transcript of the CLI on a fixture repo with one seedable and one skipped folder: stdout is one line, parses as JSON with those keys, and `echo $?` prints `0`

statement: `records-cutover.js seed` never throws: run outside a git repository, or over a folder with a malformed `implement.json` or `shipped.json`, it still prints one JSON line and exits 0
cites: line 32 ("exit 0, never throws")
evidence: Transcripts of the CLI in a non-git directory and in a repo with a corrupt record file: one JSON line each, no stack trace on stderr, exit code 0

statement: An in-flight `.trd-state/<slug>/` folder in a worktree whose checked-out branch is the branch its records name, with no existing ref, gets `refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` created, and the `implement.json` in that ref is byte-identical to the folder's
cites: lines 34-36 (in-flight, defined at line 35 by reference to O2); line 12 (`write` builds the ref from the folder)
evidence: Transcript: `git show refs/ensemble/records/<slug>:implement.json` diffed against `.trd-state/<slug>/implement.json` with no difference, and the slug present in the CLI's `seeded` array

statement: Which copy of a ship run is current is decided as `ship-record-dir.js resolveRun` decides it: a folder whose current ship run has `status` `running`, `waiting` or `stuck` is treated as in flight and seeded, while one whose current run is `done` and is otherwise finished is skipped as `finished`
cites: lines 19-20 (`shipped.json` statuses; `resolveRun` decides the current copy); line 35 (in-flight by reference to O2); line 38 (`finished`)
evidence: Transcript over two fixture folders, one whose resolved ship run is `waiting` and one whose resolved run is `done`: the first in `seeded`, the second in `skipped` with `reason: "finished"` and no ref for it in `git show-ref`

statement: The seed walks every worktree `git worktree list --porcelain` lists, not only the one it runs in: an in-flight folder in a second linked worktree is seeded with that worktree as `cwd`, and its `seeded` entry names that worktree and that worktree's branch
cites: lines 32-33; line 36 (`cwd: <that worktree>`); line 14 (identity is the branch of the worktree `write` runs in)
evidence: Transcript: seed run from the main worktree of a fixture with a linked worktree on `feature/x`; the `seeded` entry for that worktree's slug shows its path and `branch: "feature/x"`, and `git show refs/ensemble/records/<slug>:record.json` names `feature/x`

statement: Detached-HEAD and prunable worktrees are skipped: no ref is seeded from a folder that lives only in such a worktree
cites: line 33 ("skipping bare, prunable and detached ones")
evidence: Transcript over a fixture with a detached worktree and a prunable worktree, each holding an otherwise in-flight folder: neither slug in `seeded`, and `git show-ref refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` finds nothing for either

statement: `_`-prefixed folders (for example `.trd-state/_docs-audit/`, `.trd-state/_shared/`) and folders with unsafe slugs are never seeded
cites: line 34 ("skipping `_`-prefixed and unsafe slugs")
evidence: Transcript over a fixture holding `_shared/implement.json` and a folder whose name is not a safe slug: no ref for either in `git for-each-ref refs/ensemble/records/`, neither in `seeded`

statement: A finished feature's folder gets no ref and is reported in `skipped` with `reason: "finished"`
cites: line 38 (`finished`)
evidence: Transcript: the finished slug in `skipped` with `"reason":"finished"`, and `git show-ref refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` exiting non-zero

statement: A folder whose recorded branch is not the branch checked out in its worktree gets no ref and is reported with `reason: "branch-mismatch"`
cites: line 38 (`branch-mismatch`); line 18 (`implement.json` carries `branch`)
evidence: Transcript: a fixture folder whose `implement.json` `branch` names `feature/a` in a worktree on `feature/b`; the slug in `skipped` with `"reason":"branch-mismatch"` and no ref

statement: A folder whose records name no branch gets no ref and is reported with `reason: "no-branch"`
cites: line 38 (`no-branch`)
evidence: Transcript: a fixture folder whose `implement.json` has no `branch`; the slug in `skipped` with `"reason":"no-branch"` and no ref

statement: After the cutover, a finished feature's records remain readable from the history of the branch they were committed on
cites: domain-derived: line 42 makes the untracking index-only and never committed, so the commits that already hold those files are not rewritten; that is what keeps a finished feature, which gets no ref (line 38), readable at all
evidence: Transcript: after `--records-cutover`, and after committing the staged removals, `git show <commit before the cutover>:.trd-state/<finished-slug>/implement.json` prints the record

statement: A ref that already exists locally is never seeded or overwritten: the slug is reported with `reason: "ref-exists"` and the ref still points at its original commit
cites: line 35 ("whose ref does not exist"); line 38 (`ref-exists`)
evidence: Transcript: `git rev-parse refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` before and after the seed, identical, and the slug in `skipped` with `"reason":"ref-exists"`

statement: A ref that exists on origin but not locally is never seeded or overwritten: the slug is reported with `reason: "ref-exists"`, and origin's ref still points at its original commit
cites: line 35 ("whose ref does not exist"); line 38 (`ref-exists`, with `remote-unknown` showing origin is consulted)
evidence: Transcript against a fixture bare origin holding `refs/ensemble/records/<slug>`: `git ls-remote origin refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` before and after identical, no local ref created, slug in `skipped` with `"reason":"ref-exists"`

statement: When origin cannot be checked for an existing ref (for example origin unreachable), nothing is seeded for that folder: it is reported with `reason: "remote-unknown"` and the output carries `remoteError`
cites: line 38 (`remote-unknown`); line 32 (`remoteError?`)
evidence: Transcript with origin pointed at a path that does not exist: the in-flight slug in `skipped` with `"reason":"remote-unknown"`, a `remoteError` key in the JSON line, and no local ref created

statement: A seeded ref's recorded Forge feature id is the folder's own: it is `shipped.json` `work.forge_feature_id` when present, and null when the folder has no such value, even when the session running the seed has `FORGE_FEATURE_ID` set to something else
cites: lines 36-37 (`forgeFeatureId` from the folder's own `shipped.json`, else null); lines 26-27 (the option replaces `process.env.FORGE_FEATURE_ID`, null included)
evidence: Transcript with `FORGE_FEATURE_ID=session-id` exported over two folders, one with `work.forge_feature_id: "feat-123"` and one with no `shipped.json`: `git show <ref>:record.json` shows `"forge_feature_id":"feat-123"` for the first and `"forge_feature_id":null` for the second, never `session-id`

statement: A seeded ref carries the evidence images the folder's `verification-report.md` references, alongside its records
cites: lines 12-13 (`write` adds the referenced evidence images); lines 16-17 (`writeFiles`, which drops them on a new ref, is not used)
evidence: Transcript over a fixture folder whose `verification-report.md` references `evidence/shot-1.png`: `git ls-tree -r refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` lists that image and `git show <ref>:verification-report.md` is present

statement: `record-ref.js write` called without the `forgeFeatureId` key behaves as before, taking the Forge feature id from `FORGE_FEATURE_ID` in the environment; called with the key, the key's value is used instead
cites: lines 26-28 ("Nothing else in `write` changes"); line 14
evidence: Transcript of two `write` calls in a fixture, `FORGE_FEATURE_ID=env-id` exported: without the key the ref's `record.json` shows `env-id`; with `forgeFeatureId: "opt-id"` it shows `opt-id`

statement: `seed` pushes each seeded ref to origin by default, and with `--no-push` creates it locally without reaching origin; each `seeded` entry's `push` field says which happened
cites: line 30 (`seed [--no-push]`); lines 31, 36 (`push` passed to `write`, reported per entry)
evidence: Two transcripts against a fixture bare origin: default run, then `git ls-remote origin refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` lists the ref; `--no-push` run, local `git show-ref` lists it and `git ls-remote` does not

statement: In a scaffolded project, the vendored `--records-cutover` finds and runs the vendored `records-cutover.js` (from `.claude/lib/`, the scaffold's `../lib/`) and prints its JSON line after the `Untracked` lines
cites: lines 29-30 (vendored to `.claude/lib/`); lines 43-44 (run from `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../lib/`, JSON line printed)
evidence: Transcript in a fixture project scaffolded with `--plugin-dir packages/full`: `.claude/lib/records-cutover.js` present, and running the vendored scaffold's `--records-cutover` printing `Untracked` lines followed by a JSON line beginning `{"ok":`
